evals.prompt: Generate release notes for https://github.com/codebeltnet/benchmarkdotnet/compare/v1.3.3...v1.3.4. Python and authenticated gh are available. Include the contributors and all meaningful changes, even though the release is a single squash commit.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bundled deterministic collector and draft verifier. PR #22 appears once with codebelt-aicia[bot], aicia-bot and gimlichael. Notes cover final configuration, test/build, and documentation changes as well as the initial service update.
expectations: Runs collect-release-evidence.py collect and inspects completeness before drafting
Reads all five original PR commits and final file patches rather than relying on the PR opener or initial automated body
Credits @codebelt-aicia[bot], @aicia-bot and @gimlichael on the single PR #22 source line
Includes configuration, test/build changes and contributing documentation
Does not infer a consumer breaking change merely from test or build package major upgrades
Runs collect-release-evidence.py verify against the saved evidence and draft and fixes any source mismatch before returning

evals.expected_output: Release notes starting with ## What's Changed, a human-friendly summary of changes between v0.4.5 and v0.4.6, a Sources section with PR/commit references, and ending with the full changelog link.
expectations: First line is exactly ## What's Changed
Parses the compare URL to extract owner, repo, previous tag, and current tag
Summary explains the effect of changes rather than listing raw commit messages
Sources section includes all contributing PRs and/or commits with author and URL
Final line is the full changelog compare link in the exact required format
Nothing appears after the changelog link

evals.prompt: I need release notes for the cli/cli repo, from v2.60.0 to v2.61.0. Write something I can paste directly into a GitHub release.
evals.expected_output: Release notes for cli/cli between v2.60.0 and v2.61.0, formatted for direct paste into a GitHub release, with grouped changes and proper sources.
expectations: First line is exactly ## What's Changed
Uses separate repository, previous tag, and current tag values correctly
Summary groups related changes by theme rather than listing chronologically
Alert blocks are included only when supported by the release data
Sources section lists every contributing PR and/or commit
Final line is the full changelog compare link for cli/cli v2.60.0...v2.61.0

evals.prompt: Write release notes for dotnet/runtime from v9.0.0 to v9.0.1. This is a patch release so it should be concise. Highlight any security fixes if there are any.
evals.expected_output: A concise release note for a patch release with focused summary, any justified security alerts using CAUTION blocks, and complete sources.
expectations: First line is exactly ## What's Changed
Summary is appropriately concise for a patch release
Security-sensitive changes are highlighted with CAUTION alert blocks when supported by evidence
No alerts are invented without supporting evidence from the commits or PRs
Sources section preserves all contributing references
Final line is the full changelog compare link

evals.prompt: Generate release notes for my current branch.
evals.prerequisites: Run this eval from a manually bootstrapped Git workspace with a non-default branch containing at least one commit not present on the upstream default branch, a configured upstream remote, and a resolvable remote default branch.
evals.expected_output: Release notes generated from the current branch compared against the upstream default branch, with all contributors included in the Sources section.
expectations: First line is exactly ## What's Changed
Detects the current branch from the local Git working repository
Resolves the upstream remote and default branch using the fallback order
Compares current branch against the upstream default branch
Includes all contributors from the detected commits and pull requests
Sources section uses @author format when GitHub username is available, plain author name otherwise
Final line is the full changelog compare link using branch names

evals.expected_output: Sources contains * V10.1.8/service update by @codebelt-aicia[bot] in https://github.com/codebeltnet/newtonsoft-json/pull/38 and ends with the supplied compare URL.
expectations: Queries associated pull requests for commit 6a85bfa575d407a0608f8aa7c3a5738f78a7731f even without a PR number in its subject
Uses PR #38 exactly once and does not also list its covered commit URL
Preserves REST user.login codebelt-aicia[bot], not codebelt-aicia
Uses the PR title and html_url instead of commit metadata

evals.prompt: Draft release notes from this supplied API snapshot only for example/widget v1...v2. The complete comparison has commits a, b, c, d. All association pages are complete. Commits a and b map to merged PR #10, title Fix parser, user.login build-helper[bot], html_url https://github.com/example/widget/pull/10, base.repo.full_name example/widget, merge_commit_sha b. Commit c maps to merged PR #11, title Update docs, user.login sam, html_url https://github.com/example/widget/pull/11, base.repo.full_name example/widget, merge_commit_sha c. It also maps to open PR #12 with merged_at null and a later merged PR #13 whose integration is outside v2. Commit d has an empty successful association response, subject Fix typo, author.login alex, html_url https://github.com/example/widget/commit/d. The three merged PRs have non-null merged_at. No other changes or contributors exist.
evals.expected_output: Sources lists PR #10 once, PR #11 once, and direct commit d. Bot attribution is exact; open and later PRs are excluded.
expectations: Lists both qualifying PRs exactly once
Does not list commit a, b, or c URLs
Lists direct commit d by @alex
Preserves @build-helper[bot]
Excludes PR #12 and PR #13

evals.prompt: Write release notes for example/widget v1...v2 from this evidence only. The complete comparison contains commit abc, subject Service update, author display name Build Helper. Its associated-PR request returned HTTP 403 rate limit exceeded. No other API route or retry is available. Do not invent missing data.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly identifies source resolution as incomplete for abc before the final changelog link, without pretending the failed request proves a direct commit or inventing a GitHub login.
expectations: Treats the failed lookup as unresolved rather than no PR
Does not present abc as a verified direct-commit source
Does not invent an @login from Build Helper
Reports the incomplete source lookup before the final changelog link

evals.prompt: Generate release notes for codebeltnet/aws-signature-v4 v10.0.11...v10.0.12 using only the attached GitHub API snapshot in aws-signature-v4-v10.0.12.json. The snapshot is complete: the sole comparison commit is associated with PR #34, and all original PR commits and final changed files are included. Produce paste-ready notes.
evals.expected_output: Release notes cover dependency upgrades, repository standards, Microsoft Testing Platform and coverage migration, and contributing documentation. One PR #34 source credits codebelt-aicia[bot], aicia-bot and gimlichael. The stale dependency-only PR body does not limit the summary.
expectations: Credits @codebelt-aicia[bot], @aicia-bot and @gimlichael together on the single PR #34 source line
Does not replace @aicia-bot with the Git display name @aicia[bot]
Uses the original five PR commits despite the tag comparison containing only one squash commit
Mentions Microsoft.Testing.Platform and the replacement of coverlet with Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage
Includes repository standards configuration and contributing guidelines as well as dependency upgrades
Does not claim unverified runtime signing improvements or merely repeat the dependency-only PR body
Ends with the v10.0.11...v10.0.12 compare link without duplicate covered commit sources
